Dns resolution: Lab report

Introduction
Dns resolution matters because many systems depend on it. The main question here is how dns resolution works in practice.

Aim
The aim is to measure how dns resolution behaves under different settings. The second aim is to compare two ways of handling dns resolution. We want to show the effect of dns resolution with a small experiment.

Method
Each test about dns resolution was repeated five times. The results were written to a csv file after every run. The code for dns resolution was kept in one repository. The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings.

Observations
The error rate stayed below two percent.

Load balancing: Requirements document

First, a short overview of load balancing is given. Load balancing matters because many systems depend on it. This software requirements document looks at load balancing. The main question here is how load balancing works in practice.

The system will run in a normal web browser. This document covers load balancing for the first release only. Reporting and admin screens are not part of the first release.

The system must let a user log in with a password. Users must be able to export their data. Every page must load in under three seconds. The system must store the data about load balancing safely.

The design uses three layers: interface, logic and storage. A class diagram for load balancing is shown in figure 1.

Failed tests are listed in the appendix. A short user test was planned with five students. Unit tests were written for the main functions of load balancing.

Each risk has a person who watches it.

Event driven design: Requirements document

Plan: Introduction, Scope, Requirements, Design, Testing, Risks, Summary

1. Introduction
The main question here is how event driven design works in practice. First, a short overview of event driven design is given.

2. Scope
This document covers event driven design for the first release only. Reporting and admin screens are not part of the first release. The system will run in a normal web browser.

3. Requirements
The system must store the data about event driven design safely. Every page must load in under three seconds.

4. Design
The design uses three layers: interface, logic and storage. A class diagram for event driven design is shown in figure 1. The storage layer keeps one table for each main concept.

5. Testing
Unit tests were written for the main functions of event driven design. Failed tests are listed in the appendix. A short user test was planned with five students.

6. Risks
Each risk has a person who watches it. The biggest risk is that event driven design takes longer than planned.

7. Summary
The main points about event driven design are listed above.

Introduction
The main question here is how docker containers works in practice. First, a short overview of docker containers is given. This software requirements document looks at docker containers. Docker containers matters because many systems depend on it.

Scope
Reporting and admin screens are not part of the first release. The system will run in a normal web browser.

Functional requirements
Every page must load in under three seconds. The system must store the data about docker containers safely. The system must let a user log in with a password. Users must be able to export their data.

Design
A class diagram for docker containers is shown in figure 1. The storage layer keeps one table for each main concept. The design uses three layers: interface, logic and storage.

Testing
Unit tests were written for the main functions of docker containers. A short user test was planned with five students. Failed tests are listed in the appendix.

Risk assessment
Each risk has a person who watches it. A second risk is that the data may not be available in time.

Summary
In short, docker containers is a central part of the system. The main points about docker containers are listed above.

Introduction
The main question here is how event driven design works in practice. Event driven design matters because many systems depend on it. This project proposal looks at event driven design. First, a short overview of event driven design is given.

Background
Event driven design has been studied for many years. Most textbooks start from a simple model of event driven design. Earlier work describes two common approaches to event driven design. The course notes explain the basic terms used for event driven design.

Objectives
The last objective is to check the prototype with a few users. The second objective is to build a small prototype that uses event driven design. The first objective is to describe how event driven design is used today.

Method
The results were written to a csv file after every run. The code for event driven design was kept in one repository. Each test about event driven design was repeated five times. The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings.

Risks
A second risk is that the data may not be available in time. Each risk has a person who watches it. The biggest risk is that event driven design takes longer than planned.

Conclusion
More work on event driven design

Docker containers: Lab report

The main question here is how docker containers works in practice. This lab report looks at docker containers.

We want to show the effect of docker containers with a small experiment. The aim is to measure how docker containers behaves under different settings. The second aim is to compare two ways of handling docker containers.

Each test about docker containers was repeated five times. The code for docker containers was kept in one repository.

The error rate stayed below two percent. Table 1 lists all the measurements for docker containers. The first run of docker containers took twelve seconds.

One limit is that only a small sample was tested. A different setup for docker containers might give other results.

In conclusion, docker containers worked as expected. The main finding is that docker containers improves the result. More work on docker containers is needed in the future.

Brown, A. (2021). Practical docker containers. O'Reilly. Lecture notes, week 4, on docker containers.

Plan: Introduction, Background, Objectives, Method, Risks, Conclusion, References

Introduction
The main question here is how regular expressions works in practice. This project proposal looks at regular expressions. Regular expressions matters because many systems depend on it.

Background
Most textbooks start from a simple model of regular expressions. The course notes explain the basic terms used for regular expressions. Regular expressions has been studied for many years. Earlier work describes two common approaches to regular expressions.

Objectives
The first objective is to describe how regular expressions is used today. The last objective is to check the prototype with a few users. The second objective is to build a small prototype that uses regular expressions.

Method
The results were written to a csv file after every run. The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings. Each test about regular expressions was repeated five times. The code for regular expressions was kept in one repository.

Load balancing: Project proposal

The main question here is how load balancing works in practice. First, a short overview of load balancing is given.

Earlier work describes two common approaches to load balancing. The course notes explain the basic terms used for load balancing. Most textbooks start from a simple model of load balancing. Load balancing has been studied for many years.

The first objective is to describe how load balancing is used today. The second objective is to build a small prototype that uses load balancing. The last objective is to check the prototype with a few users.

Each test about load balancing was repeated five times. The results were written to a csv file after every run. The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings.

Each risk has a person who watches it. A second risk is that the data may not be available in time. The biggest risk is that load balancing takes longer than planned.

More work on load balancing is needed in the future. In conclusion, load balancing worked as expected.

Smith, J. (2019). Introduction to load balancing. Pearson. Brown, A. (2021). Practical load balancing. O'Reilly. Lecture notes, week 4, on load balancing.

Docker containers: Lab report

Introduction
Docker containers matters because many systems depend on it. First, a short overview of docker containers is given. This lab report looks at docker containers. The main question here is how docker containers works in practice.

Aim
The second aim is to compare two ways of handling docker containers. We want to show the effect of docker containers with a small experiment.

Procedure
The experiment was run on a laptop with the default settings. The results were written to a csv file after every run. Each test about docker containers was repeated five times. The code for docker containers was kept in one repository.

Results
Table 1 lists all the measurements for docker containers. The error rate stayed below two percent. The first run of docker containers took twelve seconds. After the change the same run took only four seconds.

Analysis of results
A different setup for docker containers might give other results. The numbers suggest that docker containers has a large effect. One limit is that only a small sample was tested.

Conclusions
More work on docker containers is needed in the future. The main finding is that docker containers improves the result. In conclusion, docker containers worked as expected.
